newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.Africa's Mbeki, Buthelezi to hold peace talks.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa's Mbeki, Buthelezi to hold peace talks.

text.p: South African Deputy President Thabo Mbeki will meet Inkatha Freedom Party leader Mangosuthu Buthelezi on Saturday to try to end violence between their rival parties, Mbeki's African National Congress said on Thursday.

"The ANC hopes the meeting will lend the peace process the necessary authority and legitimacy and set an example for all our people in KwaZulu-Natal to follow," an ANC statement said, adding it believed leaders of both groups wanted peace.
More than 15,000 people were killed in a decade of violence in the province that began in the mid-1980s and generally pitted Inkatha against the ANC or its surrogates.
The fighting has tapered off since all-race elections in April 1994 but still breaks out periodically.

Mbeki, in charge of day-to-day running of the country as President Nelson Mandela's scheduled retirement in 1999 draws closer, will attend the meeting in Durban with Jacob Zuma, ANC leader in KwaZulu-Natal province.
The discussions on Saturday would be the highest level talks between the two sides since meetings in the early 1990s between Mandela and Buthelezi which failed to end the violence.
In recent months Zuma and senior aides of Buthelezi have made fresh efforts to end what political analysts describe as a turf war in KwaZulu-Natal.
Inkatha won majority support in the province in the 1994 election, making it one of two of South Africa's nine provinces where the ANC does not hold power.

Buthelezi has accused the ANC of assassinating more than 400 Inkatha leaders over the years, but the ANC rejects the charge. The ANC has said its war in KwaZulu-Natal is really against white members of the former apartheid-era security forces who tried to disguise their anti-ANC activities as "black-on-black" feuding.
Inkatha was set up with the blessing of the ANC but their paths split in 1979 when Buthelezi decided to follow a path of non-violent resistance to apartheid.
Buthelezi serves as home affairs minister in South Africa's government of national unity.
